subproblem.title: Trace of (cI + F(·)v) ∘ p_P equals c·dim P + F(p_P v)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), P ⊆ E any linear subspace with orthogonal projection p = p_P (P.starProjection), c ∈ ℝ, F : E → ℝ a continuous linear functional and v ∈ E. Then the endomorphism A = c·I + F(·)v, A(u) = c·u + F(u)·v, satisfies trace(A ∘ p) = c·dim P + F(p v).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Ambient n ℓ)) (c : ℝ) (F : Ambient n ℓ →L[ℝ] ℝ) (v : Ambient n ℓ), LinearMap.trace ℝ (Ambient n ℓ) ((c • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Ambient n ℓ) + F.smulRight v).toLinearMap ∘ₗ P.starProjection.toLinearMap) = c * (Module.finrank ℝ P : ℝ) + F (P.starProjection v)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. n, ℓ ∈ ℕ; E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, a finite-dimensional real inner product space with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ = inner ℝ and norm |·| = ‖·‖. Real division by 0 is 0 (Lean convention: a/0 = 0 for every a ∈ ℝ). N = n + ℓ = dim E. P is an arbitrary linear subspace of E, k = dim P = Module.finrank ℝ P, and p = P.starProjection is the orthogonal projection of E onto P (p u ∈ P and u − p u ⊥ P for all u; hence p u = u for u ∈ P and p u = 0 for u ∈ P^⊥). F : E → ℝ is a continuous linear functional, c ∈ ℝ, v ∈ E, and A = c • ContinuousLinearMap.id + F.smulRight v, i.e. A(u) = c·u + F(u)·v. trace = LinearMap.trace ℝ E, and A ∘ p is the composite u ↦ A(p u) (as a linear map).

1. Choose an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_k of P and an orthonormal basis τ_{k+1}, …, τ_N of P^⊥. Since E is finite-dimensional, E = P ⊕ P^⊥ is an orthogonal direct sum, so τ_1, …, τ_N is an orthonormal basis of E.
2. For every linear map B : E → E, trace B = Σ_{j=1}^{N} ⟨Bτ_j, τ_j⟩, because ⟨Bτ_j, τ_j⟩ is the j-th diagonal entry of the matrix of B in the orthonormal basis (τ_j).
3. pτ_j = τ_j for j ≤ k (as τ_j ∈ P) and pτ_j = 0 for j > k (as τ_j ∈ P^⊥). Applying step 2 to B = A ∘ p gives trace(A ∘ p) = Σ_{j=1}^{k} ⟨Aτ_j, τ_j⟩.
4. For each j ≤ k, ⟨Aτ_j, τ_j⟩ = c⟨τ_j, τ_j⟩ + F(τ_j)⟨v, τ_j⟩ = c + F(τ_j)⟨v, τ_j⟩, since |τ_j| = 1.
5. Summing over j ≤ k and using linearity of F: trace(A ∘ p) = ck + Σ_{j≤k} ⟨v, τ_j⟩F(τ_j) = ck + F(Σ_{j≤k} ⟨v, τ_j⟩τ_j) = ck + F(p v), because the orthogonal projection onto P has the expansion p v = Σ_{j≤k} ⟨v, τ_j⟩τ_j in the orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_k of P. Since k = dim P, this is the claim trace(A ∘ p) = c·dim P + F(p v).
Remark (the same computation without bases, matching Mathlib): A ∘ p = c·p + G(·)v with G = F ∘ p linear; by linearity of the trace, trace(A ∘ p) = c·trace(p) + trace(u ↦ G(u)v); trace(p) = k because p maps E onto P and fixes P (Mathlib LinearMap.IsProj.trace), and the rank-one map u ↦ G(u)v has trace G(v) = F(p v) (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_smulRight). The pinned SimonGMT library contains this identity with an extra scalar b (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter04.RectifiableVarifold.trace_radialEndomorphism, take b = 1).
proof_key_steps: Orthonormal basis τ_1..τ_N of E with τ_1..τ_k a basis of P and τ_{k+1}..τ_N a basis of P^⊥
trace B = Σ_j ⟨Bτ_j, τ_j⟩; since pτ_j = τ_j (j ≤ k) and pτ_j = 0 (j > k), trace(A∘p) = Σ_{j≤k} ⟨Aτ_j, τ_j⟩
Sum: ck + F(Σ_{j≤k}⟨v, τ_j⟩τ_j) = c·dim P + F(p v)

The adapted orthonormal-basis computation proves both the scalar contribution and F(p v), including zero-dimensional subspaces; the supplied basis-free route is also supported by the pinned trace lemmas. No additional hypotheses or child dependencies are needed.

subproblem.title: Derivative of the radial field γ(|y−ξ|)(y−ξ), including the centre (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ, Euclidean inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|), γ : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹, and ξ, x ∈ E; put r = |x − ξ|. Then the vector field g(y) = γ(|y − ξ|)(y − ξ) is Fréchet differentiable at x with derivative Dg(x)v = γ(r)v + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, v⟩(x − ξ) for v ∈ E, where γ'(r)/r is read as 0 when r = 0 (Lean's a/0 = 0); in particular Dg(ξ) = γ(0)·I.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (ξ x : Ambient n ℓ), ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → HasFDerivAt (fun y : Ambient n ℓ ↦ γ ‖y - ξ‖ • (y - ξ)) (γ ‖x - ξ‖ • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Ambient n ℓ) + (deriv γ ‖x - ξ‖ / ‖x - ξ‖) • (innerSL ℝ (x - ξ)).smulRight (x - ξ)) x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. n, ℓ ∈ ℕ; E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, a finite-dimensional real inner product space with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ = inner ℝ and norm |·| = ‖·‖. Real division by 0 is 0 (Lean convention: a/0 = 0 for every a ∈ ℝ). γ'(t) denotes deriv γ t. innerSL ℝ w is the linear functional u ↦ ⟨w, u⟩; for a functional L and a vector w, L.smulRight w is the map u ↦ L(u)w; ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E is the identity I. HasFDerivAt g L x means g(x + v) = g(x) + L v + o(|v|) as v → 0 (Fréchet differentiability of g at x with derivative L). Notation: r = |x − ξ|, g(y) = γ(|y − ξ|)(y − ξ), and the claimed derivative is L_x(v) = γ(r)v + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, v⟩(x − ξ).

1. Case x = ξ. Then r = 0 and x − ξ = 0. The coefficient γ'(0)/0 equals 0 and the vector x − ξ is 0, so the claimed derivative is L_ξ(v) = γ(0)v, i.e. L_ξ = γ(0)I. For v ∈ E we have g(ξ) = γ(0)·0 = 0 and g(ξ + v) = γ(|v|)v, hence g(ξ + v) − g(ξ) − γ(0)v = (γ(|v|) − γ(0))v.
2. γ is C¹, hence continuous, and |v| → 0 as v → 0; therefore ε(v) := γ(|v|) − γ(0) → 0 as v → 0. Consequently |g(ξ + v) − g(ξ) − γ(0)v| = |ε(v)|·|v| = o(|v|) as v → 0, which says exactly that g is Fréchet differentiable at ξ with derivative γ(0)I = L_ξ. This proves the claim when x = ξ.
3. Case x ≠ ξ, so r > 0. The map y ↦ y − ξ is differentiable at x with derivative I. The map y ↦ |y − ξ|² = ⟨y − ξ, y − ξ⟩ is differentiable at x with derivative v ↦ 2⟨x − ξ, v⟩ (product rule for the inner product). Since |x − ξ|² = r² > 0 and t ↦ √t is differentiable at every t > 0 with derivative 1/(2√t), the chain rule shows that y ↦ |y − ξ| = √(|y − ξ|²) is differentiable at x with derivative v ↦ (1/(2r))·2⟨x − ξ, v⟩ = r⁻¹⟨x − ξ, v⟩.
4. γ is C¹, so it is differentiable at r with derivative γ'(r) = deriv γ r. By the chain rule, φ(y) := γ(|y − ξ|) is differentiable at x with Dφ(x)v = γ'(r)·r⁻¹⟨x − ξ, v⟩.
5. By the product rule for a real-valued function times a vector-valued function, g(y) = φ(y)·(y − ξ) is differentiable at x with Dg(x)v = φ(x)·v + (Dφ(x)v)·(x − ξ) = γ(r)v + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, v⟩(x − ξ) = L_x(v), using φ(x) = γ(r) and γ'(r)·r⁻¹ = γ'(r)/r. This proves the claim when x ≠ ξ, and with step 2 the lemma is proved.
proof_key_steps: At x = ξ the claimed derivative is γ(0)I because γ'(0)/0 = 0 and x − ξ = 0
g(ξ + v) − g(ξ) − γ(0)v = (γ(|v|) − γ(0))v = o(|v|) by continuity of γ at 0
For x ≠ ξ: y ↦ |y − ξ| = √(|y − ξ|²) has derivative r⁻¹⟨x − ξ, ·⟩ (chain rule with √ at r² > 0)
Chain rule: D[γ(|y − ξ|)](x) = γ'(r) r⁻¹⟨x − ξ, ·⟩
Product rule with y ↦ y − ξ (derivative I) gives Dg(x)v = γ(r)v + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, v⟩(x − ξ)

audit.reason: The one-line Lean proposition exactly matches the stated derivative and hypotheses. At the centre, continuity gives the required little-o remainder; away from the centre, differentiating the squared norm through sqrt and applying the chain and product rules gives the displayed continuous linear map. The proof covers dimension zero and contains no circular reliance or deferred proof construction.

subproblem.title: Pointwise tangential divergence of h·γ(|x−ξ|)(x−ξ) (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2 and 5.1)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), V any rectifiable n-varifold in E (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), h : E → ℝ, γ : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹, and ξ, x ∈ E, and suppose dim T_xV = n and h is differentiable at x. Let X(y) = (h(y)γ(|y − ξ|))(y − ξ) and r = |x − ξ|. Then div_M X(x) = h(x)(nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ(x))) + γ(r)⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x)⟩, where div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) ∘ p_{T_xV}) (V.tangentialDiv X x), ∇^M h(x) = p_{T_xV}(∇h(x)) (V.tangentialGradient h x) and q_ξ(x) = |p_{T_xV}^⊥(x − ξ)|²/r² (V.normalRadialSq ξ x, equal to 0 when r = 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (ξ x : Ambient n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n → DifferentiableAt ℝ h x → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → V.tangentialDiv (fun y ↦ (h y * γ ‖y - ξ‖) • (y - ξ)) x = h x * ((n : ℝ) * γ ‖x - ξ‖ + ‖x - ξ‖ * deriv γ ‖x - ξ‖ * (1 - V.normalRadialSq ξ x)) + γ ‖x - ξ‖ * inner ℝ (x - ξ) (V.tangentialGradient h x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. n, ℓ ∈ ℕ; E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, a finite-dimensional real inner product space with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ = inner ℝ and norm |·| = ‖·‖. Real division by 0 is 0 (Lean convention: a/0 = 0 for every a ∈ ℝ). For V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ and x ∈ E: T_xV = V.tangentSpace x is a linear subspace of E; p_x = (T_xV).starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto T_xV and p_x^⊥ = (T_xV)ᗮ.starProjection the orthogonal projection onto its orthogonal complement (p_x^⊥ = I − p_x); both are self-adjoint and idempotent. For X : E → E, div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x := trace(fderiv ℝ X x ∘ p_x), where fderiv ℝ X x is the Fréchet derivative DX(x) whenever X is differentiable at x. For h : E → ℝ, ∇h(x) = gradient h x is the Riesz representative of Dh(x) = fderiv ℝ h x, i.e. ⟨∇h(x), u⟩ = Dh(x)u for all u, and ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x := p_x(∇h(x)). q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x := |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² (= 0 when x = ξ). γ'(t) = deriv γ t. This proof uses the sibling lemmas radial_vector_field_hasFDerivAt (for γ ∈ C¹ and all ξ, x: y ↦ γ(|y − ξ|)(y − ξ) is differentiable at x with derivative u ↦ γ(r)u + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, u⟩(x − ξ), r = |x − ξ|, γ'(r)/r = 0 when r = 0) and trace_scalar_add_rankOne_comp_starProjection (for every subspace P with projection p, c ∈ ℝ, linear F : E → ℝ and v ∈ E: trace((cI + F(·)v) ∘ p) = c·dim P + F(p v)).
